claude_only.name: What minimum tuple constitutes one binding assertion, and which components are mandatory versus optional?
When must a coded value be recorded as a full binding record rather than as an inline coded attribute of the subject?
May two distinct binding records hold the same subject, scheme and term at the same time, and if so what distinguishes them?
How is an individual binding addressed and cited by an external system without dereferencing the subject?
Does this binding license any inference about the subject's type, and if not how is that non-entailment recorded?
Where a scheme term is also published as a formal class, which reading governs the binding?
Is a binding to a narrower term to be treated as also binding the subject to broader terms?
At what granularity does this binding apply: whole subject, a named part, a time slice, or an aspect?
Which subject kinds are eligible for binding under this slot, and which are explicitly excluded?
Does the subject correspond to the statistical or classificatory unit the scheme was designed to classify?
Which system is the master of record for this binding's identifier, and what identifier form does it issue?
What natural key makes repeated ingestion of the same binding idempotent?
Which external identifiers of the same binding must be carried alongside the internal one?
What is the canonical URI of the scheme, and which registry governs it?
Which scheme version was in force when the term was selected, and is the binding version-pinned or version-floating?
Is the term carried by URI, by notation, or by both, and how is a notation resolved to a term?
How is a stored display label reconciled when the scheme later changes that label?
What is the slot's stable name, the subject type it applies to, and the decision it feeds?
Which scheme fills this slot, and on what documented basis was it chosen over alternatives?
Does the permitted scheme vary by jurisdiction, tenant or process step, and how is the applicable variant resolved at runtime?
How is the permitted term set defined: by enumeration, by scheme subtree, by level, or by a computed rule?
Are non-leaf or non-selectable terms permitted, and at which classification level must the term sit?
Is a point-in-time expansion of the permitted set captured, and when is it refreshed?
May the slot draw terms from more than one scheme simultaneously?
What binding strength applies to this slot, and what validation severity does each strength map to?
Under an extensible binding, what test decides that no code in the value set can apply?
May a local profile tighten or loosen the inherited strength, and what governance approves that?
What minimum and maximum number of terms may be bound in this slot?
Is the term set mutually exclusive at the applicable level, and is multi-labelling permitted?
When several terms are bound, how is the primary or governing term determined?
What role does this applied term play: classifying, identifying, assessing or tagging?
Is the applied value a simple term reference or a post-coordinated expression, and does the scheme permit expressions?
What qualifiers modify the applied term (negation, suspected, historical, laterality, degree)?
Was this term selected directly by a person, produced automatically, inherited, or derived from a mapping?
If produced automatically about a natural person, does the binding feed a decision based solely on automated processing?
Which software serialised or generated this binding, distinct from the agent responsible for its content?
How are residual, unknown, not-applicable, refused and not-yet-classified states distinguished in the record?
Does a residual or unknown binding create a follow-up obligation, and with what deadline?
Does the scheme claim exhaustive coverage of the subject population, and what happens when it demonstrably does not?
Under which strengths is uncoded text a conformant outcome rather than a validation failure?
Is the recorded text the user's original wording or a system-generated rendering of a code?
How does recurring uncoded text become a proposal for a new scheme term?
Which agent is responsible for this binding's content, and in what capacity did they act?
Which coding method, rule set, coding index or model version produced the assignment?
Which inputs did the assignment activity consume, and are they retained for re-derivation?
At what instant did the assignment activity complete, and in which time zone was it recorded?
What concrete evidence supports the chosen term, and where is each item held?
Which interpretative rules or scheme notes were applied in reaching the term?
What is the human-readable rationale, and is it sufficient for an independent reviewer to reach the same term?
Who is entitled to assert a binding in this slot, and what qualification or delegation is required?
What force does the binding carry: advisory, internally binding, contractually binding, or legally binding on third parties?
By what route may the binding be challenged, and with what effect on its validity while under challenge?
What distinguishes annulment, revocation and cessation of validity for this binding?
What is the confidence value, on what scale, and does it represent a calibrated probability?
What acceptance threshold was applied, and what happens to assignments below it?
Which alternative terms were considered and rejected, and are they retained?
How is coding accuracy for this slot measured, over what sample and against what reference standard?
What accuracy or agreement level is required, and what happens when it is not met?
How often is quality re-measured, and what triggers an unscheduled measurement?
Which temporal frames are recorded for this binding, and what does each mean?
Over what interval does the binding assert that the subject bears the term?
How is the ingestion or observation time recorded separately from the original assertion time on import?
May a binding be asserted with retroactive or future validity, and who approves that?
How is it detected that a bound term has been deprecated, split, merged or retired in a newer scheme version?
What is the policy for bindings whose term is no longer valid: freeze, migrate, or invalidate?
When a term splits into several successors, how is the single correct successor chosen?
How is time-series or reporting continuity preserved across a scheme revision?
What is the closed set of lifecycle states, and what does each mean for a consumer?
Which transitions are permitted, who may trigger each, and what evidence must accompany them?
How does a state change interact with the validity interval and with already-published downstream data?
Is this change a correction of an error or a reclassification following a real change in the subject?
How is the supersession chain recorded so that a consumer can reconstruct the binding history?
How does an affected party register a dispute, and what does the binding look like while disputed?
Where the subject is a natural person, how is a rectification request received, decided and propagated?
What is the ordered set of checks a validator runs, and which are blocking?
What happens when the scheme or version cannot be resolved at validation time?
Is a binding to a deprecated or retired term a validation error, a warning, or acceptable for historical records?
Is the validation outcome retained as evidence, and for how long?
Which conflict types are detected, and how is each defined precisely?
When two authorities assert incompatible bindings, which prevails and on what recorded basis?
How is a cross-scheme disagreement assessed given that mappings may be inexact?
Which source binding and which mapping entry, at which mapping version, produced this binding?
What is the fidelity of the mapping used, and what information was lost?
May derived bindings be chained through multiple mappings, and how does fidelity degrade along the chain?
How is a derived binding distinguished from an original assertion in every projection?
Which exchange projections are supported, and what is the field mapping for each?
Which binding fields are lost in each projection, and how is that loss disclosed to the consumer?
Can a binding be reconstructed from a projection, and what canonical form is used for comparison?
Does this binding constitute a special category of personal data or otherwise heightened-risk information?
Who may read this binding, and is read access narrower than access to the subject record?
How long is the binding retained after it is superseded or revoked, and under what obligation?
When a binding must be erased, what remains, and how is the audit trail preserved without re-identifying the subject?

grok_only.name: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this classification-binding assertion, and which registry or terminology service issued it?
What governed global IRI, if any, identifies this binding assertion independently of storage format?
If no master-system identifier or IRI exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and when was it assigned?
Has the implementation incorrectly used the classification code, a date, or a display label as the binding identifier?
Which subject is classified, and what is its master identifier or IRI?
What kind of classifiable item is it (resource, dataset, person, organisation, variable, metadata item, geospatial record, or other)?
If the binding constrains or fills a specific element, attribute or variable, which slot on the subject is bound?
Does the binding apply to the whole subject or only to a part, version, observation or geographic coverage of it?
What canonical URI or master identifier identifies the classification scheme or code system, and has an authoritative naming system confirmed it?
What kind of scheme is referenced (controlled vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, ontology, statistical classification, or uncontrolled list)?
Does the stored system identifier point at a code system or concept scheme rather than at a value set or expansion URL?
Which organisation maintains the scheme and is it an official, community or local scheme for this binding’s jurisdiction?
What code, notation or concept IRI identifies the classification item within the scheme?
Is the combination of scheme identifier and item code unique, and is a scheme version required because the system does not guarantee concept permanence?
Is the code a precoordinated concept or a post-coordinated expression in the scheme’s syntax, and is that expression valid?
Is the concept asserted to be in the referenced scheme (skos:inScheme or equivalent), and does that assertion match the scheme URI on the binding?
What display string does the referenced scheme define for this item, in which language, and is it the scheme’s recommended display?
What text did the user or agent enter as the intended meaning, and does it stand alone without a code?
Are preferred labels unique per language within the scheme, and has any process treated display text as a computable identifier?
If no code is present, is a literal subject or keyword recorded, and is it preferred to be aligned later to a controlled vocabulary URI?
Which value-set canonical URL is bound to this element or slot, and is it version-pinned?
Is the bound object a value set rather than a code system, and which code systems does that value set draw from?
Are additional bindings defined for particular usage contexts, and what is each additional binding’s purpose?
What human-readable description states the intent of this element binding for implementers?
What binding strength applies to this slot, using the required, extensible, preferred or example codes?
If strength is required, does every populated instance contain a code from the bound expansion?
If strength is extensible and no bound code applies, what alternate coding or text was used and who reviewed that the value set did not cover the concept?
If strength is example, are instances still expected to record a scheme and code when known, rather than treating the example set as closed?
What facet or role does this binding play (subject/theme, type/genre, place, discipline, taxon, statistical variable, or other keyword type)?
Is this the primary classification for the facet, a secondary class, or an unordered additional theme?
Does the slot allow multiple simultaneous classes, require mutual exclusivity, or require a single most-appropriate class despite known overlap?
If both a type/genre and a subject/theme are recorded, are they separate bindings rather than one overloaded code?
What is the current lifecycle status of this binding assertion (proposed, active, superseded, withdrawn, historical)?
Over what inclusive start and optional end instants did this class apply to the subject, recorded as RFC 3339 date-times with seconds and an explicit offset or Z?
When was the binding observed or ingested, as distinct from the event time at which the class applied?
During a scheme revision, is a dual binding to the predecessor and successor classifications required, and which correspondence supports that pair?
If the assigned code has since been retired or combined in a later scheme version, is the historical binding preserved rather than rewritten?
Which version of the scheme was used when this code was chosen, and is version mandatory because the system requires it?
Does this scheme guarantee concept permanence across versions, and if not, what happens to historical bindings when items change?
If the item changed between versions, was the change virtual (code or name only) or a real semantic change, combination or split?
Should this binding be retargeted to a successor item, left on the original version, or dual-coded?
Which person, organisation or software agent assigned this classification, and under what role?
Was this coding chosen directly by a user from a pick list, or inferred, mapped or algorithmically assigned?
What evidence supports the assignment (observed characteristic, coding index entry, document excerpt, rule identifier)?
What confidence or quality measure accompanies an automated assignment, and is that measure standardised or locally defined?
If the assignment is automated or uses an extensible extra code, who reviewed it and with what outcome?
Who is the custodial authority of the referenced scheme, and is the URI the one authorised by that authority or by a naming system such as HL7 THO/HTA?
Which party owns this binding record in the adopting Dimension, and who may update or withdraw it?
In which jurisdiction or statistical territory is this classification valid (for example NAICS versus NACE versus ISIC)?
Is this assignment an official legal or statistical coding, a community convention, or a local convenience class?
Does the code exist in the stated system and version, and was the expansion or code-system snapshot used for the check recorded?
If a required or extensible binding applies, is the code in the value-set expansion, and what expansion identifier and timestamp were used?
Has any consumer used display or text as a join key instead of system plus code or concept IRI?
If the slot requires mutually exclusive categories, do multiple active bindings for the same facet violate that rule?
Are system URIs compared case-sensitively, and does the code system declare whether its codes are case-sensitive?
Which additional codings are translations of the same concept, and which coding is user-selected or preferred for exchange?
What mapping or correspondence, if any, justifies treating two items from different schemes as comparable on this subject?
If only a free-text keyword or literal subject is present, what controlled-vocabulary alignment is planned and who owns that gap?
When projecting to DCAT, is dcat:theme used for KOS concepts and dcat:keyword for literals, without assuming a fixed OWL range for theme?
Is this binding sensitive personal, health, or otherwise restricted classification, and which access scope applies?
Which roles may read, create, update or withdraw this binding, and what is logged?
How long must historical bindings be retained after supersession, and under what legal or statistical hold?
When is deletion of a binding permitted (for example erasure right) and what tombstone or justification remains?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
